content:
You can left-align table captions in LaTeX without the caption package using several methods:

## Method 1: Redefine `\@makecaption`
Add this to your preamble:

```latex
\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@makecaption}[2]{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    #1: #2\par
  \else
    \hbox to\hsize{\hfil\box\@tempboxa\hfil}%
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother
```

Then modify the `\hbox` line to:
```latex
\hbox to\hsize{\box\@tempboxa\hfil}%
```

## Method 2: Use `\captionsetup` equivalent manually
```latex
\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@makecaption}[2]{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  #1: #2\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother
```

## Method 3: Simple per-table solution
For individual tables, you can use:

```latex
\begin{table}[h]
\caption{\hspace*{\fill} Your caption text \hspace*{\fill}\mbox{}}
\begin{tabular}{cc}
...
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

Or more simply:
```latex
\begin{table}[h]
\caption{\raggedright Your caption text}
\begin{tabular}{cc}
...
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

## Method 4: Using `\parbox`
```latex
\begin{table}[h]
\caption{\parbox{\textwidth}{\raggedright Your caption text}}
\begin{tabular}{cc}
...
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

The first two methods will affect all table captions in your document, while methods 3 and 4 work on a per-table basis.
